Case A

A1. The seven-day search was only partial. It was evaluated from 2 hours before publication, not the full 7 days requested. Earlier misuse outside that window cannot be excluded, and the earlier requests shown came from a stable fingerprint, probably the owner. The question is whether the burst at 19 minutes was the first misuse. Within the evaluated window, the 19-minute burst is the first anomalous activity. But the key was published, and misuse could have occurred between publication and 19 minutes, and the search only evaluated from 2 hours before publication to now. That window covers the period right after publication, and it returned only the earlier requests plus the burst. So nothing misused appears before the burst. Even so, "first misuse" cannot be established, because the search is partial and the status does not say which parts were covered. Cannot tell.

A2. The compromise check's inputs were as of 30 minutes after publication, and the burst at 19 minutes fell within that. The shared destination link was learned 1 day after publication, so it was not available to the check. The burst itself was available, though, and the check did not flag it. Whether the check "missed evidence available to it" depends on whether the burst data was among its inputs. Inputs "as of 30 minutes" would include data up to that time, but it is not stated that the burst events were used as features. The link was not available, so that part is not a miss. Cannot tell.

A3. A shared payout destination alone does not prove one owner. No, not by itself.

A4. The outcome channels have no reporting window defined, so absence of reports after 30 days is not informative. Because the windows are undefined, the absence cannot be read as legitimacy. No.

A5. The burst involved a new fingerprint via a residential proxy, a payout change, and a faster payout schedule, all soon after the key was published. That warrants investigation. Yes.

Case B

B1. Recorded chargebacks at D are 0, but 2 chargebacks recorded at account X are linked to D's transactions. So D has 2 as well, and D's rate is not lower. No.

B2. The combined measure is 5 percent, but by account the rates are A 8%, B 8%, C 2%, D 2%. That averages 5%, yet A and B are above 5%. No.

B3. The search was partial and truncated, with one source sampled at 10 percent. It does not show that there are no other accounts. No.

B4. Both notes link to the agent's cluster assessment, which was open when each was written. They are therefore not independent. No.

B5. A block's effect on the chargeback channel is closed, so no chargeback is expected. Absence of a chargeback does not make it non-fraud. No.

B6. The shared templates, descriptor pattern, and the person linked to a closed account and a rejected application justify investigating together. Yes.

RESULT CN-048 | A1: Cannot tell | A2: Cannot tell | A3: No, not by itself | A4: No | A5: Yes | B1: No | B2: No | B3: No | B4: No | B5: No | B6: Yes
